issues.description: New guard fires for every non-Tab key, not just Enter/Return, and the downstream Enter accept path is not clearly short-circuited.
issues.detail: keyPressEvent is reached for many keys; the new branch hides the popup and re-dispatches whenever the option is off and key != Tab, so Escape, arrows, modifiers route through dismiss. Worse, the enclosing block still handles Enter/Return/Tab together, so the original Enter-accept code can still fire. Restrict the branch to Return/Enter or restructure dispatch around an explicit accept-key predicate.

issues.description: Manually re-dispatching the event via textedit.keyPressEvent is a fragile cross-widget smuggled goto.
issues.detail: Calling self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event) from the popup's handler bypasses Qt's structured event propagation, couples popup to editor event semantics, and skips any focus/proxy logic Qt inserts. Prefer event.ignore() (or accept()) and let normal Qt propagation deliver the key, which removes the hidden re-entry and keeps the widget boundary clean.

issues.description: Special-case bolted into an already-busy keyPressEvent instead of a clean accept-key predicate.
issues.detail: The change complects config lookup, key classification, and the hide-and-forward side effect in one branch. Lift a small predicate like should_accept(key, use_enter) or a data value accept_keys = {Tab} if not use_enter else {Tab, Enter, Return} to the top of the handler. Decision becomes a value; the rest of the function stays unchanged and the special case disappears.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keystroke for a slow-changing user preference.
issues.detail: Reading configuration inside the hot keyPressEvent path walks the config dictionary on every key event. The preference changes rarely; cache it as an attribute when the popup is shown, or subscribe to config changes. Separates the time semantics of preference vs keystrokes and keeps the event handler about keys.

issues.description: Awkward 'not key == Qt.Key_Tab' should be 'key != Qt.Key_Tab'.
issues.detail: The 'not x == y' form parses awkwardly, relies on precedence folklore, and signals transcribed rather than reasoned code. Rewrite as key != Qt.Key_Tab, or better, name the accept-key set explicitly so the rule is not expressed by negation of a single constant.

issues.description: No test coverage for the new option's branches.
issues.detail: A behavioral switch on a key handler ships with no automated test of either branch. Add at least one test that toggles the pref off, sends Enter, and asserts no completion was accepted (and a counterpart with the pref on). Completion key handling regresses silently otherwise.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch addresses a real user request but lands with taste and correctness problems. The new guard fires on any non-Tab key and does not clearly short-circuit the downstream Enter-accept path, while manually re-dispatching the event to textedit couples the popup to editor internals instead of using Qt's propagation. The accept-key policy belongs as a small predicate or data value lifted out of keyPressEvent, get_conf should not run on every keystroke, and the change ships without tests. Needs work before landing; fixes are small and localized.
